name: sol_basics_al_7
description: Missing uniqueness validation on user-supplied array allows duplicate entries to be processed
question: The source file in `source` defines a function that accepts an array (often user- or caller-supplied) and iterates over it performing state-changing operations such as accumulating balances, applying rewards, transferring funds, or removing/whitelisting items per element, without validating that the array elements are unique, so a caller can pass duplicate entries to cause unintended double-processing, inflated totals, double payouts, or bypass of limits, excluding arrays whose semantics inherently tolerate or require duplicates and arrays that are already deduplicated or validated for uniqueness before use.
criteria: distributeRewards(address[] calldata recipients) loops over recipients and adds reward amount per entry without checking for duplicate addresses, allowing a duplicated address to receive multiple rewards

batchTransfer(address[] memory to, uint256[] memory amounts) sends tokens to each address in the array without verifying uniqueness, letting a repeated address receive multiple transfers from a single call

addLiquidityForPools(uint256[] calldata poolIds) increments a counter or updates state for each poolId without checking poolIds for duplicates, letting a repeated poolId inflate the counter or state improperly

removeWhitelist(address[] calldata users) or similar bulk-update function processes each entry and updates a mapping/count without deduplicating the input, allowing repeated entries to double-decrement or corrupt shared counters
